_note: Planning doc — master session-by-session tracker for the reboot campaign. NOT a live entity. Sits alongside campaign_arc.json's phase-goal breakdown; this file tracks what actually happens session-by-session as it gets designed, which doesn't necessarily land on the phase boundaries campaign_arc.json originally sketched (see pacing_target.caveat below).

pacing_target.decision: CONFIRMED (2026-08-01) — roughly 10 sessions per phase, 30 sessions total. Session 1 is Phase 1's opener.
pacing_target.caveat: In practice, session-level design for Sessions 1-5 already surfaces material originally scoped as Phase 2 (Corvin's identity, the Thornwick connection, Torvald as the insider) well before a notional 'session 10' Phase 1 climax. Treat the phase documents (phase1/phase2/phase3_*.json) as content reference libraries, not strict session-number gates — this file is the authoritative session-by-session record when the two disagree.

session_1.status: PLAYED IN FULL (2026-08-09) — see content/sessions/session_1.html's 'What Actually Happened at the Table' DM-only note for how actual play diverged from the design (tunnel fight instead of open field, harder-than-expected fight, an unresolved unnamed figure Torvald was seen talking to). session_1.beats: Parting gifts montage, the Voss summons/office scene, recruitment pitch as Ninth Thesis operatives (accepted outright by all four, ~50gp/week), a corrupted bulette (ambient veil-bleed, NOT possession — no independent entity riding it, just abnormal aggression/toughness from proximity to the destabilizing veil, ties to campaign_arc.json's 'occasionally something leaks through' premise) fought underground after burrowing, debrief.
session_1.correction_2026-08-02: The bulette is CORRUPTED, not possessed — word choice matters: 'possessed' implies an intelligence behind it that isn't there.

session_2.status: PLAYED 2026-08-20, reconciled against the transcript 2026-08-23. content/sessions/session_2.html is now the record of what happened and is authoritative over session2_draft.html and over these beats. data/sessions.json category Planning → Completed; reveals: [prof_bram_holdar]; visibility deliberately held at dm-only pending the leak decision recorded at the foot of session_2.html. DID NOT RUN: Voss's contact list (DM forgot it — being delivered retroactively at the top of Session 3), the Celestial spoken trigger word (scrapped; the glyph fired on the package being opened), and the escape. Session 2 ends stranded on the Thanatos platform with ~15 armanites a minute out. Session 3 now opens there, and the Neverwinter Wood arrival plus the four-direction fork both slide one session later.

post_session_2_fork.status: SLIPPED ONE SESSION (2026-08-23) — the premise is intact but the timing is not. Session 2 was played on 2026-08-20 and the party never reached Neverwinter Wood: both escape routes failed and they ended the session still standing on the Thanatos platform. The fork therefore does NOT happen at the top of Session 3. Session 3 is now the escape from the platform (the dais and its forked rod, still untouched, are the only remaining exit) plus the arrival in Neverwinter Wood; the four-direction choice moves to the top of Session 4. Everything below is otherwise unchanged and still correct — including that the rod is set to the Neverwinter Wood delivery lane, which is why they land there and which quietly seeds Thundertree. Original note, still true when it happens: the party is stranded not knowing where they are, and must pick a direction with zero information about what's actually there.

directions.south: The Triboar Trail — the original planned route; still leads toward the same Triboar/Yartar-adjacent territory session_2 used to cover directly.

post_session_2_fork.prep_status: None of the four are detailed yet — explicitly beyond Session 2's scope per the DM. Only prep whichever one the table actually picks, once Session 2 is played and the choice is known.

session_3.status: PUSHED (2026-08-23) — these beats are now Session 4 at the earliest. Session 3 is no longer 'arrival in Neverwinter': it opens ON THE THANATOS PLATFORM, mid-scene, under a stated ~1-minute clock with roughly fifteen armanites inbound, because Session 2's escape failed. Session 3's actual content is (a) Voss's contact list handed over retroactively as a flashback beat, (b) the escape — the central dais and its forked rod are the only exit left, the drow's scroll having been destroyed, and everything the party failed to examine on 2026-08-20 is still physically within reach during a fighting retreat, (c) the drow, still unnamed and entirely unspent, who may or may not come with them, and (d) the arrival in Neverwinter Wood. The four-direction fork then opens Session 4. PRIOR NOTE, still applicable to whichever session finally carries these beats: the 'arrival in Neverwinter' framing below assumed a deliberate, chosen departure from campus, which session_2 no longer delivers. If the party picks south (the Triboar Trail) out of Neverwinter Wood, this beat sheet likely still applies with minor rework. If they pick west, northwest, or east instead, this session needs to be redesigned around whichever location that turns out to be — do not assume Neverwinter arrival until the Session 2 table's actual choice is known.

graduation_ring_selection.status: RESOLVED — options list live since 2026-08-05 (content/references/rings.html, sixteen patterns including the 2026-08-13 homebrew Ring of Augury); staging drafted 2026-08-14 in session2_draft.html as a public part of Commencement, doubling as the diploma conferral.
graduation_ring_selection.concept: A graduation tradition: every graduate selects one magic ring from a menu of options. All the rings are physically identical regardless of choice — plain, bearing the Academy crest — so the effect is a private/mechanical choice, not a visible status marker.
graduation_ring_selection.content_approach: CONFIRMED — reused existing D&D ring options (e.g. Ring of Protection, Ring of Mind Shielding) rather than inventing from scratch, plus one homebrew addition (Ring of Augury). The Ring of Augury is now published as a D&D Beyond homebrew magic item (2026-08-18): https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11893776-ring-of-augury — linked from content/references/rings.html and content/references/dnd_resources.html, so players can add it to their character sheets.

geography.academy_location: CORRECTED (2026-08-15, DM ruling — supersedes the earlier 'Evermoors border, southeast of Silverymoon' reading taken off the hand-drawn route map). The Academy sits INSIDE the High Forest but only just, at the forest's northwestern-most edge, roughly 200 yards south of the River Rauvin. Silverymoon is about two days' walk NORTH (not south-southwest). Consequence: north of campus the trees give out almost immediately and open onto the river; south and east the forest runs on for days and deepens. This is now reflected in live data — campus_root.html, high_forest.html, river_rauvin.html, silverymoon.html.

Ring of Augury (homebrew ring, added 2026-08-13 to content/references/rings.html, one of the Registrar's approved graduation-ring patterns; published to D&D Beyond 2026-08-18 at https://www.dndbeyond.com/magic-items/11893776-ring-of-augury) — mechanically a 1/day action-cast augury via warm/cold answers, deliberately unclear in-fiction who or what is actually answering. RESOLVED (2026-08-18, DM ruling): Archcleric Senna makes the rings herself and every one is bound to a single deity — SAVRAS, god of divination and truth. Rationale is a countermeasure to the sealed chapels: a named, portable channel a sealed room can't reach, plus a god who cannot answer falsely, which makes a wrong answer proof of interception rather than bad luck. Recorded DM-only in content/npcs/archcleric_senna.html; deliberately absent from all player-facing content (rings.html says only that the source is not evident from wearing it). Set aside in reaching this: Ninth Thesis backing, a Thornwick/cult surveillance vector echoing Torvald's ring, ambient veil-bleed, a fully unconnected mystery. STILL OPEN: whether/when the interception actually happens to a PC's ring, and what the entity wants from the exchange (see archival_prayer_text.html).

None of the six are revealed and none belong in session_2's reveals[]. CLOSED (2026-08-23): Session 2 Celestial trigger word. SCRAPPED at the table on 2026-08-20 — the DM ran the glyph as firing on the package being OPENED, not on a spoken word. Nobody read the note aloud; Silas got one word off it while crossing the room and Guntrah tore the box open before he could stop it. No trigger word is owed and none will be. Everything else about the beat held: package addressed to the groundskeeper, Common note hiding it from Voss, Celestial text nobody read, 20 ft radius, DC 20 CHA, one-round window to follow (used by Guntrah and Tito, who both resisted and chose to jump; Silas and Tavian were taken). NEW OPEN ITEM arising from this: the original design's cleverest clue — that the trap only catches someone literate enough to be a threat, and is therefore inert to Osric and Torvald — is no longer supported by the mechanism as run, since anyone can open a box. Decide whether that inference is still available to the party by another route before it matters.

Ring Conferral staging (2026-08-23, arising from play): the Conferral was restaged live on 2026-08-20 and diverges from the locked 2026-08-14 version in three ways — the rings are visibly DIFFERENT METALS rather than struck identical, they are labelled and openly displayed so every choice is public rather than a quiet 'Pattern?' to a clerk, and SEPARATE DIPLOMAS exist (handed out by a graduate assistant), so the ring does not double as the diploma. There was no clerk, no folio, and no enchanted stylus; Dowe handled it herself and commented approvingly on two of the four picks. content/references/rings.html still describes the old staging. RESOLVED (2026-08-24, DM ruling — and the ONE case in this pass where the authored data overrules the transcript). The recording renders the Conferral as an on-stage pick from a case of mixed-metal, individually-labelled bands; the DM has clarified that was never the intent. CANON: selection is PRIVATE and happens BEFORE Commencement, with the full list in front of the graduate and as long as they want — the whole point being that nobody should have to read item descriptions or ask rules questions on a stage. The ceremony is where the choice is ANNOUNCED. Bands stay as originally authored: struck identical, gold (plated or solid), crest to the face, year inside — appearance is explicitly not something the DM cares to vary. What the transcript DOES settle and is now canon: separate diplomas exist and are conferred by a clerk alongside the Headmistress, so the ring does NOT double as the diploma (superseding the 2026-08-14 restaging), and Dowe reads choices out with a remark attached. Knock-on, unchanged: 'a ring reveals nothing about its wearer' still holds by SIGHT, but the pattern is not a secret — anyone at that Commencement heard it announced. content/references/rings.html rewritten accordingly. Ring choices themselves are recorded on the PC entities: Guntrah Swimming, Silas Regeneration, Tavian the Ram, Tito Free Action. Nobody took the Ring of Augury, so the Savras/Senna thread is entirely unspent.
